title: Cheat Sheet
markdown:
## Which document (milestone 1)

| You want to | Read |
|---|---|
| learn something new | a tutorial, then explanation |
| get a task done | a how-to guide, then the reference for each call |
| know exactly what a call does | the reference page |
| know what is allowed, finally | the specification or standard |
| know what changed | the changelog, release notes, migration guide |

## A reference page, in reading order

1. **Synopsis**: find the overload you are calling.
2. **Description** and **Parameters**: your arguments, including empty, zero, null, negative, too large.
3. **Return value** and **Errors**: every outcome.
4. **Notes / Remarks**: always skim.
5. **Requirements**: version, header, library, platform.

| Word | Means |
|---|---|
| must, shall, requires | a rule for you |
| may | allowed to happen: be ready for it |
| unspecified | one of several results, no promise which |
| implementation-defined | the compiler or library chooses and documents it |
| the behaviour is undefined | breaking this voids everything |

## C++ signatures and contracts

| You see | It means |
|---|---|
| `const T&` | read, no copy |
| `T&` | your object is changed |
| `T&&` | may be moved from |
| `[[nodiscard]]` | do not ignore the result |
| `noexcept` | never throws |
| `[first, last)` | half-open: `last` excluded |
| `InputIt`, `RandomIt` | named iterator requirements |
| strong guarantee | on throw, nothing changed |

## Standard library results (milestone 2)

| Call | "Not found" / failure |
|---|---|
| `std::find`, `map::find` | the end iterator |
| `string::find` | `std::string::npos` |
| `map::insert`, `try_emplace` | `.second == false`: key existed, nothing changed |
| `map::insert_or_assign` | `.second == false`: key existed, value overwritten |
| `std::from_chars` | `ec != std::errc{}`; check `ptr` reached the end; no `+`, no spaces |
| `std::stoi` | throws `invalid_argument` / `out_of_range`; skips spaces; stops at junk |
| `std::filesystem` (two overloads) | throws `filesystem_error`, or sets `std::error_code&` |

| Container | Invalidated by insertion |
|---|---|
| `vector`, `string` | all, if it reallocates; else at and after the point |
| `deque` | all iterators, not references (at the ends) |
| `list`, `map`, `set` | nothing |
| `unordered_*` | all iterators on rehash, not references |

Erase in a loop: `it = c.erase(it);`, or `std::erase_if(c, pred)`.

Versions: `(since C++20)` markers, `/std:c++20`, `__cpp_lib_*` macros from `<version>`, `_MSVC_LANG`.

`std::format` spec: `{:fill align sign # 0 width .precision type}`; numbers align right, strings left.

## Windows pages (milestone 3)

| Prefix / annotation | Means |
|---|---|
| `cch`, `nSize` "in characters" | count of `wchar_t` |
| `cb` | count of bytes |
| `_In_`, `_In_opt_` | read; `_opt_`: null allowed |
| `_Out_writes_(n)` | buffer holds `n` elements |
| `_Out_writes_bytes_(n)` | buffer holds `n` bytes |

| Unknown size pattern | Example |
|---|---|
| ask for the size (null buffer) | `GetEnvironmentVariableW`: too small returns size **with** null; success returns length **without** |
| grow until it fits | `GetModuleFileNameW`: returns `nSize` when truncated |
| size in, size out | `RegQueryValueExW`: `ERROR_MORE_DATA` (234) |

| Error system | Test |
|---|---|
| last error | `GetLastError()` immediately after a documented failure |
| return code | `ERROR_SUCCESS` (0) is success |
| `HRESULT` | `SUCCEEDED(hr)` is `hr >= 0`; `0x8007xxxx` = Win32 error `xxxx` |
| `NTSTATUS` | top bits: `00` success, `01` info, `10` warning, `11` error |

Structures: zero-initialise (`{}`), set `cbSize = sizeof(...)`, reserved members zero. "One or more of" = flags with `|`; "one of" = a single value.

## Other languages and specifications (milestone 4)

| Source | Watch for |
|---|---|
| Python | `/` positional-only, `*` keyword-only; "Changed in version"; in place vs new object |
| MDN | Syntax lines, Exceptions, Browser compatibility, Baseline |
| Node | Stability index; callback, promise and sync variants; `err.code` |
| headers | defaults, `const`, pointers vs references, `///` comments |
| man pages | section number; RETURN VALUE; ERRORS |
| RFCs | MUST / SHOULD / MAY; ABNF; errata; obsoleted by |

## From docs to code (milestone 5)

1. Run the example unchanged. 2. Look up every call. 3. Make it a function. 4. Add every error path. 5. RAII for every resource. 6. Loop for partial results. 7. Test the edges.

Experiment: one question, predict first, smallest program, edge cases. Keep it as a learning test. Undefined behaviour proves nothing.
